site.name: orbitride
site.summary: orbitride-clone Fictional intercity rideshare / bus booking flow "OrbitRide". Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Landing: search box (From / To city autocomplete datalist, date, passengers) + 3 value props + 6 popular-route cards | | `routes.html` | Trip results list: left filters (time-of-day, price slider, 4 amenities multi-select); top 7-day date carousel; 8 trip rows (carrier, departure–arrival, duration, stops, amenities, seats left, price, Select button) | | `seats.html` | SVG bus seat map: front 2 priority rows, middle 11 standard 2+2 rows, rear 5-seat row; selectable count = passengers; occupied / selected / standard / priority states; right side legend + selected list + price box + Continue |

run_plan.goal: Exhaustively explore the OrbitRide booking funnel from landing search through confirmation, while also validating adjacent discovery/filtering behavior, seat-selection constraints, and key recovery/backtracking paths on both desktop and mobile.
run_plan.summary: The run should follow the visible end-to-end purchase flow: landing search on index.html, trip selection on routes.html, seat selection on seats.html, then complete the remaining checkout pages passengers.html, extras.html, payment.html, and confirmation.html. Along the way, it should probe the most consequential stateful controls already seen in the prescan, especially route filters, date carousel, Select actions, and passenger-count-to-seat-count constraints. Mobile validation should focus on the booking-critical path and the prescan’s small tap-target risks in the header/navigation and compact controls.
assumptions: The primary journey is a linear booking flow across index.html → routes.html → seats.html → passengers.html → extras.html → payment.html → confirmation.html, based on the available HTML files and page purposes.
The landing page search form likely seeds route context into routes.html, since routes.html visibly shows origin/destination/date/passenger summary text.
Seat selection is constrained by passenger count, because the prescan explicitly states selectable count = passengers on seats.html.
Header links Help and Sign in appear to be non-navigating placeholders in prescan (href '#'), so they should be checked for UX impact but not treated as full flows.
Popular route cards on index.html are visible content, but the prescan did not confirm them as clickable, so they should only be tested if interactable during execution.
risk_hotspots: index.html search form: FROM/TO/date/passengers combination and Find rides submission
index.html header links (Routes, Help, Sign in): tiny tap targets already flagged in prescan
routes.html query summary showing 'null → null · null · 2 passengers' in prescan, indicating possible missing state/default-data issues
routes.html filters: departure-time select, max-price slider/input, and four amenity toggles
routes.html 7-day date carousel: verify date switching and consistency of results/prices
routes.html repeated Select buttons across 8 trip rows: ensure clear row targeting and stable navigation
seats.html SVG seat map: occupied/selected/priority/standard states and seat-count enforcement tied to passenger count
seats.html Continue action: verify blocked vs enabled progression depending on valid seat selection
Checkout transition pages passengers.html, extras.html, payment.html: high-risk for data carryover and summary consistency because they are downstream but not prescanned
Mobile header and dense booking controls across index/routes/seats due to existing small tap target warnings and likely compressed layouts

phases.title: Entry and search initiation
phases.objective: Validate that the landing page clearly supports trip search and that users can begin the booking flow with plausible inputs and understandable defaults.
key_checks: Review initial clarity of the hero/search module and whether the default-filled or entered values are legible and sensible
Exercise FROM and TO inputs using visible route examples where possible
Change DATE and PASSENGERS values, including a multi-passenger case to set up downstream seat-count testing
Submit via Find rides and confirm navigation to routes.html
Check whether header links and brand link behave coherently without derailing the main flow
If popular route cards are clickable in execution, test at least one as an alternate route-entry path
exit_criteria: At least one successful search reaches routes.html
One alternate search state or changed passenger count has been attempted
Landing-page navigation and top-level controls have been sanity-checked for obvious dead ends or UX confusion

phases.title: Route discovery and refinement
phases.objective: Validate the results-list browsing experience, the usefulness and reliability of filters, and the ability to choose a trip with confidence.
key_checks: Inspect the search summary at top for preserved origin/destination/date/passenger data and note any null/missing-state defects
Use the departure-time select and verify that visible results respond plausibly
Adjust the max-price control and confirm pricing/result changes are understandable
Toggle each visible amenity filter at least once, plus a multi-filter combination
Use the 7-day date carousel to switch dates and verify results/prices or state updates
Compare at least two trip rows with different carriers/stops/amenities/seats-left messaging
Activate Select from more than one row context if feasible, ensuring the selected trip is the one that advances
exit_criteria: Filters, date carousel, and at least one Select action have been exercised
The run has evidence on whether route context is preserved correctly
A chosen trip progresses to seats.html

phases.title: Seat-map constraint validation
phases.objective: Deeply validate the most stateful interaction in the prescan: seat selection rules, visual states, and progression gating.
key_checks: Inspect legend and seat-map readability across occupied, selected, standard, and priority seats
Attempt to select seats up to the passenger-count limit established earlier
Attempt over-selection beyond the passenger limit and verify prevention or messaging
Test deselection/reselection to ensure state updates and selected-seat list remain synchronized
Compare behavior of priority rows versus standard seats, including whether restrictions or pricing differences are communicated
Check price box updates as seats are chosen
Test Continue with invalid/incomplete selection versus valid selection
exit_criteria: Seat-count enforcement has been positively validated
Seat-state transitions and pricing/summary updates have been observed
Continue successfully advances only after a valid seat selection

phases.title: Checkout completion pages
phases.objective: Traverse and critique the downstream booking steps for continuity, clarity, and data carryover through completion.
key_checks: On passengers.html, verify presence and usability of traveler-detail entry and whether selected trip/seat summary remains visible
On extras.html, inspect optional add-on choices and whether opting in/out is clear and reversible
On payment.html, verify payment form structure, required-field affordances, and booking-summary consistency
Complete the purchase path to confirmation.html if possible using available demo inputs
On confirmation.html, check for a clear success state and final trip/passenger/seat/payment recap
exit_criteria: All remaining known checkout pages have been visited
End-to-end booking reaches confirmation.html or a blocking defect is documented with the failing step
At least one continuity check has been made at each step for summary/data preservation

phases.title: Recovery paths and mobile regression
phases.objective: Validate that the flow tolerates backtracking and that the critical journey remains usable on a mobile viewport.
key_checks: Use browser/page backtracking between booking steps and confirm key selections are retained or loss is understandable
Repeat the booking-critical interactions on mobile: search initiation, route filtering/selection, seat selection, and at least one checkout form step
Re-check header/nav controls on mobile because prescan already flagged small tap targets on index.html
Assess whether dense controls on routes.html and the seat map on seats.html remain operable without overlap or accidental taps
Confirm any final confirmation/success information is readable on mobile without major clipping
exit_criteria: Critical path has been spot-checked on mobile through at least seats.html and one downstream checkout page
At least one recovery/backtrack scenario has been executed
Mobile-specific usability issues and tap-target/layout concerns have been documented

coverage_targets.pages: Visit all 7 known HTML pages, with deeper repeat coverage on index.html, routes.html, and seats.html because they expose the most visible interaction complexity.
coverage_targets.features: Exercise the full visible booking path plus most visible controls on key pages: landing search fields and submission, route filters/date carousel/Select actions, seat-map selection states and Continue, and at least the main forward actions on passengers/extras/payment/confirmation pages.
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat the critical booking checks on a mobile viewport for index.html, routes.html, seats.html, and one downstream checkout page, with special attention to the already-flagged small header tap targets and dense stateful controls.

notes: Do not assume modal dialogs, account flows, or real help/sign-in experiences because none were evidenced in prescan.
If routes or downstream pages expose validation or disabled states naturally, capture them; but do not fabricate unsupported scenarios.
Given max_steps=80 and exhaustive depth, spend proportionally more time on routes.html and seats.html than on marketing content.

ux_notes: Clicking the OrbitRide logo on mobile seats navigates directly from seats.html back to index.html, so it does function as an escape hatch back to search.

The return drops users onto the generic landing/search page with no visible explanation, saved-progress message, or seat-selection context in the observed text, which can make backtracking feel abrupt when users were trying to recover from an incomplete seat step.
On the destination page, the OrbitRide logo tap target is only 119x28px and flagged below 44px mobile guidance, reducing reliability of this recovery path on touch devices.

step.objective: Learn whether tapping the OrbitRide logo on the mobile landing page behaves predictably or feels like a redundant/dead navigation element.
step.success_criteria: The tap either keeps the user on the same page with no feedback, or causes a reload/clear state, revealing whether the homepage logo is redundant, inert, or disorienting on mobile.

result.feedback: No obvious URL or visible-text change was detected after the action.
